architectureDecisions: D1 — The supported v1 distribution is one single-tenant OCI/container profile with a CLI-first control surface. Kubernetes tenancy, multi-node HA and an operator web UI are explicitly deferred; they require separate measured product need.

D2 — The normative release identity is DELIVERY_RELEASE_MANIFEST_V1 binding ExHarness source/release version, OCI image digest, Node runtime major, state-schema compatibility version, supported SCM=GitHub, supported runtime adapter/profile refs and required configuration keys. Mutable tags are never sufficient release identity.

D3 — Node 24 is the supported runtime major for this profile because the current repository kernel CI executes on Node 24. The container image carries the runtime; a clean operator host requires Docker/Compose-compatible container execution and Git, not a matching host Node installation.

D4 — The supported operator CLI commands are doctor, configure, run, status, cancel, backup, restore and upgrade-check. They compose BB-070 lifecycle and BB-072 operations APIs; the CLI is an adapter/control surface and owns no alternate lifecycle or acceptance state.

D5 — Configuration is schema-validated and split from secrets. The committed config example contains no credentials; provider/SCM secrets enter only through named environment/file secret inputs. doctor fails with actionable typed errors for missing credentials, unsupported runtime, unreachable SCM/provider prerequisites and incompatible persisted state.

D6 — Clean install consumes only the pinned release bundle: compose.yaml, config example/schema, release manifest and runbook. Installation must not depend on a developer checkout, prior session state or unpublished local files.

D7 — Upgrade is allowed only after upgrade-check validates state-schema compatibility and either no ACTIVE/RECOVERY_REQUIRED attempt exists or the exact delivered compatibility contract permits continuation. Otherwise the operator must quiesce/cancel/reconcile first. No in-place best-effort migration is allowed from an unknown state.

D8 — Rollback uses the exact previous OCI digest plus its compatible state snapshot/release manifest. If the current persisted schema is not rollback-compatible, rollback requires restoring the pre-upgrade backup; unsupported downgrade fails closed.

D9 — OpenHands software-agent-sdk v1.49.6 is not repackaged as a second product; the distribution consumes the exact BB-070/BB-069 delivered runtime profile. Langfuse v4.46.0 remains optional observability infrastructure from BB-072 and is not required for install/health.

D10 — Worker preflight requires BB-070 and BB-072 DONE and binds their exact lifecycle/operator/config/state compatibility outputs. Any mismatch in control commands, canonical data roots or compatibility semantics is PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION.

expectedDependencyOutputs: BB-070 DONE: exact supported product-entry/lifecycle/reference-product API and release identity consumed by the distribution.
BB-072 DONE: exact operator CLI/API, canonical store roots, backup/restore contract and state-schema compatibility metadata consumed by install/upgrade/rollback.

implementationSlices: S0 — Dependency/profile preflight: require BB-070 and BB-072 DONE; bind exact lifecycle/operator APIs, canonical data roots and compatibility metadata; reject mismatch as PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION.

S1 — Release manifest/config: implement DELIVERY_RELEASE_MANIFEST_V1 and config schema/example, bind immutable image digest/runtime/schema/SCM/runtime-profile identities and typed required secret names.

S2 — CLI package: create @exharness/delivery-cli with doctor/configure/run/status/cancel/backup/restore/upgrade-check as thin adapters over delivered application/operations boundaries; add negatives proving the CLI cannot directly edit canonical state.

S3 — Container profile: build one Node-24 single-tenant image and compose.yaml with explicit data/config/secret mounts, healthcheck and immutable release-manifest exposure; no Kubernetes/operator UI path.

S4 — Clean-room install exercise: from an empty temp host directory, use only the packed release bundle/runbook/config to start the profile and complete the BB-070 reference delivery; record exact image/release/config identities and actionable failures.

S5 — Compatibility exercise: test missing credentials, unsupported runtime metadata and incompatible persisted state; run supported upgrade-check, quiescent upgrade and exact-digest rollback with pre-upgrade backup/restore when schema rollback requires it.

S6 — Distribution integrity: pack the CLI/workspace artifacts, scan the clean-room bundle for undeclared developer-checkout dependencies/secrets/mutable image identity and verify supported commands against a fresh operator process.
S7 — Update Living truth and runbook with exact supported profile, prerequisites, support boundaries, upgrade/rollback rules and known exclusions.

researchEvidence.finding: Current kernel CI uses Node 24; the supported distribution profile pins Node 24 inside the container rather than requiring operator-host Node.
The runtime remains a delivered upstream dependency/profile, not a separately repackaged lifecycle product inside BB-073.
Observability UI/backend is optional and unnecessary for the minimum install/run/health/upgrade control path; BB-073 remains CLI-first.
A separate packages/delivery-cli workspace package plus OCI bundle is the smallest distribution seam without changing core-harness or agentic runtime ownership.
